snippet.title: What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn? 💍
snippet.description:
Look up: a giant glowing arch across the sky, nights that never get dark, and a ring shadow that brings colder winters. 💍 And the strangest part? Earth may really have had rings once.

An imagined scenario with simplified science, just for fun.

FACT CHECK
• Earth may have had a ring around 466 million years ago (Ordovician), formed from a broken-up asteroid: Tomkins, Martin & Cawood (2024), "Evidence suggesting that earth had a ring in the Ordovician", Earth and Planetary Science Letters 646, 118991. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.epsl.2024.118991
• The same study suggests the ring's shadow may have helped cool the planet. How rings would look from different latitudes (a thin line overhead at the equator, a wide arch from mid-latitudes) follows from simple geometry of rings above the equator.
